questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. A boy tended his master’s dogs near a pond.

B. However, he realized that the way he talked to them never made them happy.

C. Soon he found the tending and his life there very boring.

D. All he could do to kill the boredom was by talking to the dogs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "ACDB".**
​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'A' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about "a boy". Hence, 'A' is the first part.
 
• The verb "tending" in the sentence 'C' refers back to the verb 'tended**' mentioned in the sentence 'A'. Hence, 'C' follows 'A'.
 
• The noun 'boredom' in the sentence 'D' refers back to 'boring' mentioned in the sentence 'C'. Hence, 'D' follows 'C'.
 
• The verb 'talked' in the sentence 'B' refers back to 'talking' mentioned in the sentence 'D'. Hence, 'B' follows 'D'.

 

After rearranging the sentences__: *A boy tended his master’s dogs near a pond. Soon he found the tending and his life there very boring. However, he realized that the way he talked to them never made them happy. All he could do to kill the boredom was by talking to the dogs.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question:
**Directions: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

Our twenty-first-century society expects all relevant information to simply be handing to us.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"handing to us"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the **form of the verb** 'handing' is **incorrect**.
 
• The **given sentence** is in the **passive voice** as in the passive voice, there are **only the verb and the object**, no subject to be mentioned.
 
• We form the **passive** with **be + past participle** (third form of the verb).
 
• Therefore, the **present participle** form '**handing**' should be **replaced by** the **past participle** form '**handed**'.
 
• **Hence**, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence__:** *Our twenty-first-century society expects all relevant information to simply be **handed to us**.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Vishnu said, "I am going to the theatre this evening."

options.text: Vishnu said that I am going to the theatre this evening
Vishnu said that he would go to the theatre that evening.
Vishnu said that he was going to the theatre this evening.
Vishnu said that he was going to the theatre that evening.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Vishnu said that he was going to the theatre that evening**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or ____converting direct speech into indirect speech__:​
 __
 
• The **commas and inverted commas** are **removed**.
 
• The second person 'I' will be changed into 'He'. The pronoun 'this' becomes 'that'.
 
• The present continuous tense format '**Subject + am + V1 + ing + Object**' will be changed into the past continuous tense format '**Subject + was + V1 + ing + Object**'.
 
 
 
• From the following rules, we get the correct sentence as- option 4*.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

__So much as__ you behave like this, the decision of the management against you cannot be revoked.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "​as long as".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given underlined segment, the use of "So much as" is incorrect as "so...as" can only be used with negative like 'not'.
 
• We use not + so + adjective/adverb + as to make comparisons, meaning not to the same degree.
 
• But we use as + adjective/adverb + as to make comparisons when the things we are comparing are equal in some way.
 
• We use "**as long as"** to **refer to the intended duration of a plan or idea, most commonly referring to the future**. We always** use the present simple to refer to the future **after** "as long as".**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct Sentence__: ***As long as** you behave like this, the decision of the management against you cannot be revoked.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• We can use "as...as" for both negative and positive, "so...as" can only be used with negative.
